record_notes.DCP-LETT-1222: February 6 with supplied 1849 year. Acknowledges missing current Fox note and water-cure information, while two Fox condolence notes were seen but not necessarily addressed to Darwin. Recalls father last visit, remains undecided about Malvern and asks whether Fox cases involved dyspepsia. Suppressed gout is Holland attributed historical assessment, not established diagnosis. Gully book must be obtained, not already read. Fruit-tying advice was tried; embedded Lindley/Gardeners Chronicle instruction is a short quotation of a missing communication, not a complete prompt. Reports prior summer success for some pears/plums, including ninety pears on one tree; apricots/peaches now experimental. Missing Fox health/fruit input does not match preserved 1846 goose fragment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1235: March 24 with supplied 1849 year, at Malvern. This day fortnight supports March 10 arrival under assigned date; May departure possibilities remain uncertain. Credits Fox for expedition, describes current treatment and subjective improvement, but sweating process begins tomorrow. Do not treat planned treatment as already performed or historical efficacy claims as verified modern medicine. Invites Fox later April; six children/servants/governess present, irritation expected to disappear but outcome not yet known. Raw MathML bedtime is eight and a half, not flattened 812. No surviving current incoming Fox prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1240: April 18 with supplied 1849 year. Thanks missing note a fortnight ago, approximate interval rather than exact arrival April 4. Plans end-of-May release and hopes June 1 arrival at Down; later actual June 30 return must not overwrite this contemporary expectation. Reports thirty days without sickness, weight gain, seven miles yesterday and recent relaxed treatment; these are personal observations. Gully patient count is hearsay and wealth inference. Athenæum and glacier paper need not be sent until Down return; this does not establish present receipt or reading. Editorial identifications of article/paper are alternatives or conjectures. No current Fox letter body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1249: July 7 with supplied 1849 year, Saturday. Returned last Saturday, supporting June 30 actual arrival, after sixteen rather than six weeks; distinguish from earlier June 1 expectation. Continues regimen, building douche, anticipates a year of treatment. Considers sickness absolutely cured, a contemporary belief qualified by other symptoms and later relapse; raw twelve hours without flatulence is literal integer, no MathML fraction. Credits Fox, reminds promised summer visit and considers Birmingham meeting prospectively. Later November visit is editorial outcome, not knowledge at July 7. Historical views about water cure and slavery remain attributed Darwin prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1292: Thursday January 17, 1850 inferred from child born day before yesterday, independently identified January 15. Mr Wood is Charles Henry Lardner Woodd, Fox brother-in-law, not Searles Valentine Wood the naturalist. Offers to answer yet unspecified questions; no answer content invented. Describes own administration of chloroform before doctor arrival and perceived effect: historical narrative, not present clinical guidance. Explicitly answers missing Fox water-cure question and says health better than during Fox visit; visit known completed by this date, while November 2 exact visit day is supplied separately by diary apparatus. Reports fossil cirripede work. No preserved prompt matching these current topics.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1323: Thursday in May 1850, not an independently chosen exact day. Responds to missing Fox caution about harmful water-cure cases; regularly reports to Gully and changes treatment, does not endorse treating himself without guidance. Wants Fox doctor opinion while acknowledging individual uncertainty. Recently improved after six-week retrograde period, qualifying earlier absolute cure language. Chloroform comments attributed to Simpson/own contemporary opinion; do not convert to clinical truth. Egerton farm praise came orally weeks earlier, not from a preserved incoming Fox letter. Gully visit desired but travelling resisted; no accomplished trip implied.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1352: September 4 with supplied 1850 year. Missing Fox letter supplied heredity and nail-shedding facts; Darwin hypothetical taxonomic judgment is not a verified new species. Agassiz racial polygenism is attributed and queried as possible source of questions, with comment on slavery; do not silently label it Darwin adoption. Fox remedy aphorism is explicitly quoted. Health improved against two years ago but not fully cured. Bruce Castle inspection planned for Friday, not yet performed; asks Fox information. Quetelet remark about untreated comparison read recently, potentially through Herschel review according to apparatus; no proof entire Quetelet book read or earlier availability. Gully daughter recovery is reported anecdote involving several treatments, no causal proof. Later George Darwin recollection in apparatus is not contemporary body knowledge. Delayed Athenæum bundle mention does not securely establish direction, receipt or content reading.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1362: October 10 with supplied 1850 year. Missing juicy Fox letter includes Bruce Castle sentence and home education, riding and pear questions. School choice still undecided though leaning Bruce Castle; later Rugby decision in 1852 must remain future. Reports Willy falls without stirrups, asks advice not yet received. Fox farm knowledge includes earlier oral Egerton praise. Summer visit and eighth child midsummer anticipated, not accomplished. Australia/America emigration speculation is not a completed move or settled plan. Wall pears fruitful, standards fruitless, now doubts besom treatment for standards; this revises 1222 optimism. Rivers dwarf trees planted following older advice. Pamphlet offered, editorial identification only probable. No current Fox prompt survives among checked sources.
